treatment_rationale.summary: Trastuzumab targets confirmed HER2-positive disease. Select the treatment setting first: an early-breast course has a planned endpoint; metastatic therapy follows disease control and tolerability.
treatment_rationale.line: Early disease: part of the agreed perioperative anti-HER2 course. Metastatic disease: establish the previous regimen and intended continuation plan.
factors: Confirm HER2 testing, treatment intent, previous anti-HER2 exposure and cardiac suitability.
Count prior trastuzumab within the early-breast total course; do not restart a new year automatically.
Review surgical response and residual disease before choosing postoperative continuation.
alternatives: Residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant treatment requires assessment of an appropriate post-neoadjuvant strategy, including NCCP 00659 where eligible.
For metastatic treatment, choose the contemporary HER2 strategy using prior exposure, disease pattern and current local access; HERA does not establish this choice.
treatment_rationale.limitations: This card covers two settings. The HERA evidence below applies only to early breast cancer and does not compare modern metastatic options.

sources.label: NCCP 00200 v8 — IV trastuzumab every 21 days
Cameron et al., HERA final follow-up, Lancet 2017
NCCP 00659 v2 — T-DM1, residual early breast

evidence_at_a_glance.population: HER2-positive early breast cancer after primary therapy; 5,099 patients in the intention-to-treat population across three arms.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: One year of three-weekly trastuzumab versus observation after chemotherapy and other primary therapy.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: EARLY BREAST ONLY. These figures must not be presented as the effect of metastatic trastuzumab or of the remaining maintenance infusions alone.

endpoints.definition: HERA study-defined DFS composite; includes breast-cancer events, non-breast malignancy and death without a preceding event. Not interchangeable with iDFS.
endpoints.interpretation: Improved DFS in the early-breast trial population.
endpoints.limitations: Observation-arm crossover complicates the untreated comparison.

sources.label: Cameron et al., HERA final follow-up, Lancet 2017

endpoints.result_text: Lower mortality hazard with one year of trastuzumab.
endpoints.definition: Time from randomisation to death from any cause.
endpoints.interpretation: OS benefit supported; no fixed-time absolute OS figure is supplied here.
endpoints.limitations: An HR is not an absolute survival percentage.

sources.label: Cameron et al., HERA final follow-up, Lancet 2017

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: Two years did not improve DFS over one year.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Secondary cardiac endpoints occurred in 4.4% with one year versus 0.9% with observation.
limitations: 52% of the observation group selectively crossed over to trastuzumab.
This historical comparison does not select between current post-neoadjuvant regimens.

sources.label: Cameron et al., HERA final follow-up, Lancet 2017
NCCP 00200 v8 — IV trastuzumab every 21 days

treatment_rationale.summary: Weekly IV trastuzumab provides HER2-directed treatment for metastatic disease. The reason for monotherapy and the weekly schedule should be explicit in the individual treatment plan.
treatment_rationale.line: Historical directly matching evidence: disease progressed after one or two chemotherapy regimens. The NCCP card itself does not establish a universal preferred line.
factors: Confirm HER2 positivity, previous systemic therapy, response, cardiac function and whether the plan is ongoing monotherapy or continuation after combination therapy.
Use the weekly protocol and its continuation/loading instructions; do not inherit the three-weekly indication text.
alternatives: Review combination or other HER2-directed options against current NCCP eligibility, prior exposure and patient suitability.
If considering a different interval or formulation, use its separate protocol; a shared target does not make administration instructions interchangeable.
treatment_rationale.limitations: A single-arm historical response study cannot establish a survival gain or comparative modern treatment preference.

sources.label: NCCP 00201 v6 — IV trastuzumab every 7 days
Cobleigh et al., weekly monotherapy, JCO 1999

evidence_at_a_glance.population: 222 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer progressing after one or two chemotherapy regimens.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Single-arm study: 4 mg/kg loading dose, then 2 mg/kg weekly; no randomised control.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Directly matches the weekly single-agent schedule, but describes previously treated progressive metastatic disease, not a separately tested maintenance population.

endpoints.definition: Complete plus partial responses assessed by an independent committee in the intention-to-treat population.
endpoints.interpretation: Activity demonstrated; no comparative response gain can be calculated.
endpoints.followup: A median follow-up duration is not specified in the retrieved abstract.
endpoints.limitations: No comparator, hazard ratio or absolute treatment difference. Response is not cure.

sources.label: Cobleigh et al., weekly monotherapy, JCO 1999

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: Responses could be durable; the study does not establish a comparative survival advantage.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Cardiac dysfunction occurred in 4.7%; infusion fever/chills were common, usually mild or moderate and concentrated at the first infusion.
limitations: Do not import chemotherapy-plus-trastuzumab survival results as a monotherapy effect.
Historical population and treatment sequence limit direct application to contemporary practice.
The 2023 republication is not a new trial or a new efficacy analysis.

sources.label: Cobleigh et al., weekly monotherapy, JCO 1999
NCCP 00201 v6 — IV trastuzumab every 7 days

treatment_rationale.summary: T-DM1 combines HER2 targeting with a cytotoxic payload for eligible advanced disease previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane.
treatment_rationale.setting: HER2-positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
treatment_rationale.line: NCCP 00206a: prior trastuzumab and taxane, plus prior advanced-disease therapy or recurrence during/within six months of adjuvant therapy.
factors: Check previous HER2 treatments, recurrence interval, disease distribution, cardiac function, platelets, liver tests and neuropathy.
Distinguish metastatic NCCP 00206 from the finite post-neoadjuvant course in NCCP 00659.
alternatives: DESTINY-Breast03 directly favoured T-DXd over T-DM1. EMILIA does not establish T-DM1 as universally preferred over modern options.
Sequence treatment using prior exposure, CNS disease, contraindications and current NCCP access; access was not verified by this evidence audit.
treatment_rationale.limitations: EMILIA compared against lapatinib/capecitabine in a historical treatment sequence, not against every current HER2 option.

sources.label: NCCP 00206 v5 — T-DM1, advanced breast
Verma et al., EMILIA primary report, NEJM 2012
Diéras et al., EMILIA final descriptive OS, Lancet Oncology 2017
DESTINY-Breast03 long-term analysis, Nature Medicine 2024

evidence_at_a_glance.population: 991 patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Advanced-disease evidence. Do not transfer these results to postoperative residual disease or assume the same effect after all modern preceding therapies.

endpoints.definition: Time from randomisation to death from any cause.
endpoints.interpretation: Longer OS than the trial comparator.
endpoints.limitations: 27% of control patients crossed to T-DM1. These are the final-analysis medians, not the 2012 interim medians.

sources.label: Diéras et al., EMILIA final descriptive OS, Lancet Oncology 2017

endpoints.definition: Time from randomisation to progression or death, assessed by independent review.
endpoints.interpretation: Longer PFS than the trial comparator.
endpoints.followup: Earlier analysis than the final OS report
endpoints.limitations: Do not combine this endpoint's analysis label with final-OS follow-up.

sources.label: Verma et al., EMILIA primary report, NEJM 2012

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: The randomised trial supports efficacy against its named comparator; contemporary selection also requires newer direct comparisons.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Thrombocytopenia, hepatotoxicity and neuropathy remain important T-DM1 considerations; cardiac and pulmonary toxicity also require protocol-based assessment.
limitations: Metastatic evidence does not establish adjuvant benefit.
Median differences describe trial distributions, not an individual's expected additional survival.
Later treatment sequencing differs from the EMILIA era.

treatment_rationale.summary: Residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant HER2-directed treatment identifies a postoperative escalation decision rather than routine trastuzumab continuation.
treatment_rationale.setting: NCCP 00659a: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease in breast and/or nodes after neoadjuvant taxane/HER2 therapy.
treatment_rationale.line: Post-neoadjuvant adjuvant treatment after surgery; a planned 14-cycle course if tolerated.
factors: Confirm the exact NCCP residual-disease, HER2, previous-treatment and postoperative eligibility criteria.
Review pathology, previous toxicities, platelet/liver results, neuropathy and cardiac suitability.
Coordinate postoperative radiotherapy and endocrine treatment where indicated through the agreed multidisciplinary plan.
alternatives: KATHERINE compared T-DM1 with trastuzumab continuation.

DESTINY-Breast05 subsequently favoured T-DXd for iDFS in a high-risk residual-disease population; consider current evidence, toxicity and verified local access rather than describing T-DM1 as superior to all current options.
treatment_rationale.limitations: This is not the pathway for pathological complete response or all early HER2-positive disease. A newer publication alone does not amend NCCP access criteria.

sources.label: NCCP 00659 v2 — T-DM1, residual early breast
Geyer et al., KATHERINE final iDFS / second interim OS, NEJM 2025
DESTINY-Breast05, NEJM 2026

evidence_at_a_glance.trial: KATHERINE — final iDFS and second interim OS
evidence_at_a_glance.population: HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive breast/axillary disease after neoadjuvant taxane-based chemotherapy and trastuzumab.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: 14 cycles of T-DM1 versus 14 cycles of trastuzumab.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Post-neoadjuvant residual invasive disease only. Not a generic adjuvant or pathological-complete-response estimate.

endpoints.definition: Time from randomisation to invasive breast-cancer recurrence, including contralateral invasive disease, or death.

sources.label: Geyer et al., KATHERINE final iDFS / second interim OS, NEJM 2025
KATHERINE 2025 author-institution abstract

endpoints.definition: Time from randomisation to death from any cause.
endpoints.interpretation: OS improvement supported at the second interim analysis.
endpoints.analysis_status: Second interim OS, published 2025 — not final OS
endpoints.limitations: Unstratified HR; do not label this a final OS analysis.

sources.label: Geyer et al., KATHERINE final iDFS / second interim OS, NEJM 2025
KATHERINE 2025 author-institution abstract

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: This direct comparison supports escalation over trastuzumab in the studied residual-disease setting.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Grade 3 or higher adverse events: 26.1% with T-DM1 versus 15.7% with trastuzumab.
limitations: Do not transfer the trial's absolute benefits to patients without residual invasive disease.
Newer T-DXd evidence addresses a defined high-risk group and changes the alternatives discussion; it is not an automatic local-access decision.

DESTINY-Breast05, NEJM 2026

treatment_rationale.summary: Continue pertuzumab/trastuzumab after the chemotherapy component ends in an eligible responding advanced-disease patient, maintaining HER2-directed treatment while avoiding ongoing chemotherapy exposure.
treatment_rationale.setting: NCCP 00726a: HER2-positive metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable breast cancer maintenance.
treatment_rationale.line: Continuation after pertuzumab/trastuzumab with docetaxel, weekly paclitaxel or vinorelbine; not a new treatment line solely because chemotherapy stops.
factors: Confirm the preceding combination, response, reason chemotherapy ended, interval since the last antibody doses and cardiac suitability.
Continue according to the protocol until progression or unacceptable toxicity; do not apply the early-breast one-year endpoint.
alternatives: Progression requires reassessment of the systemic treatment plan rather than automatic unchanged continuation.
DESTINY-Breast09 supplies newer first-line comparative evidence for T-DXd/pertuzumab; this is not an automatic reason to switch a stable maintenance patient or a statement of Irish reimbursement.
treatment_rationale.limitations: CLEOPATRA supports a docetaxel-containing strategy; it does not quantify the independent value of maintenance or every permitted chemotherapy backbone.

sources.label: NCCP 00726 v3a — pertuzumab/trastuzumab maintenance
Swain et al., CLEOPATRA end-of-study, Lancet Oncology 2020
DESTINY-Breast09, NEJM 2026

evidence_at_a_glance.population: 808 patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, no previous chemotherapy/biological treatment for metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Pertuzumab/trastuzumab/docetaxel versus placebo/trastuzumab/docetaxel, followed by antibody continuation.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: STRATEGY-LEVEL EVIDENCE. The trial did not randomise maintenance separately. These effects cannot be assigned to maintenance alone.

endpoints.definition: Time from initial strategy randomisation to death from any cause.
endpoints.interpretation: Long-term OS benefit for the complete pertuzumab-containing strategy.
endpoints.limitations: No maintenance-only randomisation; comparator included active trastuzumab and docetaxel.

sources.label: Swain et al., CLEOPATRA end-of-study, Lancet Oncology 2020

endpoints.definition: Time from initial strategy randomisation to progression or death, assessed by independent review.
endpoints.interpretation: Longer PFS for the complete pertuzumab-containing strategy.
endpoints.followup: Data cutoff 13 May 2011; earlier than final OS follow-up
endpoints.limitations: Not a maintenance-only effect; do not substitute later investigator-assessed PFS numbers.

sources.label: Baselga et al., CLEOPATRA primary PFS, NEJM 2012

endpoints.definition: Kaplan–Meier overall survival at eight years from strategy randomisation.
endpoints.interpretation: A second view of the same OS endpoint, not independent additional benefit.
endpoints.limitations: 95% CI: pertuzumab 31–42%; control 19–28%. Does not isolate maintenance.

sources.label: Swain et al., CLEOPATRA end-of-study, Lancet Oncology 2020

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: Antibodies continued until progression; docetaxel was given for six cycles or longer at investigator discretion.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Use antibody-specific maintenance risks, including cardiac dysfunction, infusion reactions and diarrhoea. Chemotherapy-inclusive trial neutropenia rates do not describe antibody-only maintenance.
limitations: NCCP permits preceding docetaxel, paclitaxel or vinorelbine combinations; the numerical CLEOPATRA effect was not separately established for each.
Fifty control patients crossed to pertuzumab; the end-of-study analysis retained initial randomisation.
These results are not a direct comparison with contemporary first-line alternatives.

guardrails: Never load numerical trial efficacy into patient-facing bundles.
Keep early/metastatic and monotherapy/combination/maintenance populations separate.
Never construct a control arm for single-arm response data.
Preserve endpoint-specific maturity and analysis dates.
Verify local access separately from trial publication.
